record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: For sampling from a convex body using only a separation oracle, can the reflection walk be analyzed to show substantially better oracle complexity than the ball walk, potentially O*(nD) oracle calls in general and even O*(n) for isotropic bodies?

evidence.quote: It is possible that for this process, the number of oracle calls (not the number of Markov chain steps) is only O*(nD) rather than O*(n^2D^2), and even O*(n) for isotropic bodies. It is a very interesting open problem to analyze the reflection walk.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body given only by a separation oracle: on input $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the oracle either reports that $x \in K$, or returns a hyperplane separating $x$ from $K$. Assume $K$ contains a unit ball and is contained in a ball of radius $D$. Consider the "reflection walk" for sampling (approximately) the uniform distribution on $K$: from a current point $x \in K$, pick a random direction (or velocity), move along a straight line, and whenever the trajectory would exit $K$ reflect specularly off the boundary (computed via the separation oracle), continuing for a prescribed total length, then output the resulting point as the next state.

(a) Provide a mixing-time analysis of the reflection walk showing that, to produce an approximately uniform sample from $K$, the total expected number of separation-oracle calls is $\widetilde{O}(nD)$ (hiding logarithmic factors and dependence on the error parameter), substantially improving upon the $\widetilde{O}(n^2 D^2)$ oracle-call bound that follows from the standard ball walk.

(b) Strengthen the bound to $\widetilde{O}(n)$ separation-oracle calls in the case that $K$ is in (near-)isotropic position, i.e., the uniform distribution on $K$ has identity covariance.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., 2024–2025) on oracle-based uniform sampling from convex bodies (proximal samplers, In-and-Out, Dikin walks) has improved oracle complexities under various oracle models, but no source found provides the specific reflection-walk analysis achieving $\widetilde{O}(nD)$ separation-oracle calls in general or $\widetilde{O}(n)$ for isotropic bodies. The status of this specific reflection-walk question appears to remain unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Oracle-based Uniform Sampling from Convex Bodies
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms based on proximal samplers using projection/separation oracles, matching iteration complexity of In-and-Out and the Ball walk.
status_evidence.claim: Recent oracle-based samplers improve complexity but do not specifically analyze the reflection walk to the targeted bounds.

status_evidence.title: In-and-Out: Algorithmic Diffusion for Sampling Convex Bodies
status_evidence.snippet: New diffusion-based sampler for convex bodies with improved mixing analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Progress on convex body sampling complexity exists, but distinct from reflection-walk analysis.
